messages:
anya: Quick heads-up — I'm seeing a sustained spike in NVIDIA Xid 13 and 31 errors from us-west2 GPU pool (pool-12) over the last 12h. ~7% of inference pods hit GPU errors and restart. Posting the tail of kernel logs we collected from one affected node:

anya: ```
[Mar 12 03:14:22] NVRM: Xid (13): Clamp fault 0x4 at 0x12345abc, PID 4123 
[Mar 12 03:14:22] NVRM: Xid (31): Channel exception on 00000000:03:00.0 0x00000002
[Mar 12 03:14:22] GPU 0: ECC single-bit corrected errors increased: 122 -> 180
```

kyle: Which workloads are on those nodes? any shared tenants or big-batch jobs?

anya: I ran a quick query against our request logs + scheduling overlay. Most correlated failures are from rwdx-rerank-2b long-decode jobs and a smaller spike from batch-embedder-4x. The teams are different (search + recs).

anya: Prometheus snippet (12h increment):
```
increase(gpu_driver_xid_total{code="13"}[12h]) by (node)
node-12: 48
node-17: 32
node-21: 12
```

samir: Looks like a mix of Xid 13 (ECC/DRAM) and 31 (channel / scheduler). Could be thermal or a flaky card. Any recent driver/kernel rollouts?

maria: No driver pushes in the last 10 days. The only config change was a larger batch cap we enabled for rerank (max_batch_tokens=4096) on March 11.

anya: I also pulled nvidia-smi ECC counters across devices on node-12: 
```
GPU 0: ecc.corrected.volatile 580 -> 760 (12h)
GPU 1: ecc.corrected.volatile 10 -> 12
GPU 2: ecc.uncorrectable 0
```

kyle: That delta on GPU0 is concerning. Suggest cordon+drain GPU0 host and shift rerank to nodes with lower ECC deltas ASAP. Can infra coordinate? @infra-oncall

infra-oncall: Acknowledged. I'll cordon node-12 and evict pods. gpu-ops-bot will trigger a drain window; ETA ~6m.

gpu-ops-bot: Started drain of node-12. Evicting 14 pods. Fallback routing enabled to region-replica pool. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

samir: If we see repeated ECC increments after warm reboot, it's likely hardware. Plan: cordon -> reboot -> recheck counters -> if counters keep growing, schedule replacement with vendor RMA.

maria: Here's node inventory for affected hosts (short):
- node-12: p4d-1a, gpus: [0000:03:00.0 GTX-TeslaA], kernel 5.15.0-80
- node-17: p4d-1b, gpus: [0000:03:00.1 GTX-TeslaA], kernel 5.15.0-80

anya: Note: rwdx-rerank-2b runs continuous beam search with KV cache > 48MB per shard; suspect long-lived attention state + large token batches increase ECC stress. We saw similar pattern in a smaller incident last year but with Xid 79. This time it's 13/31.

kyle: Can we throttle max_batch_tokens for rerank in the short-term? Setting to 2048 might cut stress ~40% per our perf model. Also enable per-request prefix caching to reduce decode length.

maria: Changing batch config for that service now (rolling): setting max_batch_tokens=2048 for the rerank ingress. Will monitor.

anya: After cordon/reboot of node-12, ECC delta dropped on subsequent checks but node-17 still rising. Collecting GPU diag via vendor tool (dcgmi) now and will attach logs to ticket INF-6391.

gpu-ops-bot: Vendor diagnostic started (ticket INF-6391). Upload ETA 15m.

infra-oncall: If vendor diag shows memory faults, we'll schedule replacement windows next week (non-urgent if perf stabilized). For now proceed with config throttles + draining high-error hosts.

samir: For triage notes: next steps
- run extended memory test on node-17 (after offload)
- capture dmesg/driver logs + nv-hostengine logs
- map failures -> tenant + model (we already have that)
- consider adding alert for ECC delta > 100 in 6h

anya: Agreed. Adding alert rule here:
```yaml
expr: increase(ecc.corrected.volatile[6h]) > 100
for: 30m
labels:
  severity: page
```

kyle: Good. Also add label to alerts so we can auto-fence node in the pool if severity=page and count > 1 in 24h.

maria: Rolling config change applied. Early telemetry shows ~37% fewer Xid hits from rerank traffic (10m sample).

anya: Thanks all. I'll consolidate logs and write a short postmortem draft if node replacements proceed. Filing INF-6391 with links to raw logs and correlation queries.

kyle: Thanks — ping here when vendor diag completes. :thumbsup:

gpu-ops-bot: Vendor diag uploaded to INF-6391 at https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-6391/files.

anya: Follow-up: vendor diag indicates one DIMM thermal anomaly on GPU0 on node-17; scheduling replacement for next maintenance. Closing immediate surge — monitoring for 24h.

infra-oncall: Closing loop here. Marking as mitigated. Keep alerting enabled and we'll track recurrence.
